decisions.reason: The rye country bread is a core-range product on existing production lines, so holding it costs little and nothing suggests weak demand.
The repeatedly gold-medalled premium raisin stollen is the firm's flagship, and its value has largely been confirmed, so further commitment is justified.
The seeded rye mixed bread is a cheap variant on established recipes with no negative signals, so the option stays open.
The dark malt rye bread overlaps with other rye breads, which makes it the likeliest candidate for pruning, but its holding cost is low and no evidence of weak demand has appeared.
The marzipan stollen complements the core seasonal stollen business at minimal extra cost, so it is worth keeping for another Christmas season.
The ancient grain bread is the firm's promoted newest 'masterpiece' and serves a growing health-oriented niche, so its uncertain upside justifies keeping it.
